issues.legal_issue: A statutory direction that a tenure-holder’s interest devolves subject to personal law applies the personal law in force when succession opens, rather than fixing that law as of the enactment of the direction.
material_facts: The deceased held an interest as a tenure-holder, and the governing land-revenue provision directed that the interest pass subject to the holder’s personal law on death.
The deceased died after the Hindu Succession Act had come into force, and the parties disputed whether succession was governed by that Act or by the earlier Mitakshara law.
The Supreme Court found it unnecessary to decide whether the land-revenue provision was itself a law for the devolution of tenancy rights within the saving clause of the Hindu Succession Act.
issues.conclusion: The reference to personal law included the Hindu Succession Act in force when the deceased died and succession opened; the reference was not limited to Hindu law as it stood when the land-revenue code was enacted.
issues.legal_principle: A general reference to the law governing a subject adopts that law as it stands when applied, including later amendments, unlike a specific incorporation fixed at the time of adoption. The Court relied on Sutherland’s Statutory Construction and Corpus Juris Secundum for this principle. It applied that principle to Section 151 of the Madhya Pradesh Land Revenue Code, 1954, whose words ‘on his death’ indicated that personal law as amended up to the date of death governed. The Court did not decide whether Section 151 fell within the saving clause in Section 4(2) of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956; it held that Section 151 itself referred the matter to personal law.

rule.if: inheritance_dispute and tenure_holder_interest and personal_law_referred_to_generally and succession_opened_after_later_law

predicates.inheritance_dispute: The parties disputed who inherited an interest after its holder died.
predicates.tenure_holder_interest: The deceased held the disputed land interest directly from the State as a tenure-holder.
predicates.personal_law_referred_to_generally: The governing land-holding rule referred generally to the holder’s personal law without fixing it to a named enactment or date.
predicates.succession_opened_after_later_law: The deceased died after a later body of succession law had come into force.
predicates.personal_law_in_force_at_succession_appl: The personal law in force when succession opened governs the inheritance.

issues.definition: When an inheritance dispute concerns a tenure-holder’s interest, the governing rule refers generally to personal law, and succession opens after a later body of succession law has come into force, the personal law in force when succession opens applies.

issues.legal_issue: When a female intestate inherited property from her husband and died without descendants, the husband’s heirs are identified by treating him as having died immediately after her, so a relative in the applicable statutory class may succeed ahead of more remote agnates.
material_facts: The deceased female died intestate and without a son or daughter, and the disputed land had been inherited from her husband.
The claimant was the daughter of the husband’s sister; the competing claimants were the husband’s remote agnates.
Neither side fell within Class I of the applicable schedule, while a sister’s daughter was listed in Class II.
The dispute arose in an inheritance suit, and the Supreme Court affirmed the decree granting the claimant the land rights.
issues.conclusion: The husband’s heirs were to be ascertained as if he had died intestate immediately after the female intestate. The claimant, as a Class II heir of the husband, therefore succeeded in preference to the competing agnates.
issues.legal_principle: Section 15(2)(b) of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, applied because the female intestate had inherited the property from her husband and left no son or daughter. Rule 3 of Section 16 required the husband’s heirs to be determined as if he had died intestate immediately after the female intestate. Under Section 8 and the Schedule, a sister’s daughter is a Class II heir, whereas agnates are reached only after Class I and Class II heirs are absent.

rule.if: female_intestate_succession_case and property_inherited_from_husband and female_died_without_descendants and claimant_is_husbands_class_ii_relative and competing_claimants_are_husbands_agnates

predicates.female_intestate_succession_case: The proceeding concerns distribution of a female intestate’s estate.
predicates.property_inherited_from_husband: The female intestate had inherited the disputed property from her husband.
predicates.female_died_without_descendants: The female intestate died without a son or daughter, including the children of any predeceased son or daughter.
predicates.claimant_is_husbands_class_ii_relative: A claimant was a relative of the husband who fell within the applicable Class II of heirs.
predicates.competing_claimants_are_husbands_agnates: The competing claimants were agnates of the husband.
predicates.claimant_precedes_competing_agnates: The claimant who is the husband’s Class II relative succeeds ahead of the competing agnates.

issues.definition: If a female intestate’s estate includes property inherited from her husband, she died without descendants, and a claimant is the husband’s Class II relative while the competing claimants are his agnates, the claimant precedes the agnates.
